content.text: Single continuous cinematic camera move, no cuts. Stylised painterly 3D illustration with the graphic language of a hand-painted game world - bold silhouettes, simplified sculpted forms, soft painterly surfaces without fine photoreal texture detail, and light modelled in clear shapes rather than flat even illumination. Never photorealistic and never live-action, but equally never comic or cartoon. Deep violet and midnight-blue base, structures and light in royal and electric violet. Warm orange only for lamplight, backlight and rim light, never as a colour of the network. Soft bloom, volumetric haze, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, calm slightly surreal atmosphere. No text, letters, logos, icons or symbols of any kind ever appear anywhere; the sheets of paper stay completely blank. The dragonfly stands still on the stack of blank white paper on the desk, seen from behind and slightly above, her wings folded. She is a precision-engineered machine of dark chrome and anodised violet with large faceted eyes and long transparent wings veined with glowing violet nodes - elegant, constructed, never cute or cartoonish. She rises onto her legs and lifts her body, and then she opens: her chrome plates and the segments of her body slide smoothly apart along fine seams, her folded wings fan out and separate, and the joints of her frame hinge open like a precision instrument unfolding - calm, controlled and deliberate, never violent and never breaking apart. Inside her, revealed between the opened plates, lies pure violet light: the whole network she has carried with her from the very beginning. That light now streams out of her in every direction at once. It floods across the stack of paper, races out over the desk, runs up the walls and pours through the entire space, spreading faster and brighter, filling more of the frame with every moment. Fine violet lines and glowing nodes race outward through everything, folding over each other, until at the end the image is almost entirely filled with brilliant violet and white network light from edge to edge. Through it all the dragonfly stays visible at the centre of the frame, her opened form a dark silhouette held against the blaze of light. Nothing is destroyed and nothing breaks: the paper, the desk and the room stay whole underneath, and only the light is new. Everything that lights up stays permanently lit and never fades, dims or goes dark. The camera holds on the dragonfly, which stays visible and centred throughout, and never pulls back and never loses her. The shot ends with the dragonfly still clearly in frame at the centre, her form open, the whole image around her filled with glowing violet network light.
